answer: The protocol requires each agent to maintain 1,000 unique data shards for identity, verified by unpredictable retrieval audits. An honest agent incurs a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 times that expense to mirror distinct content. Like a thin thread of data, the verifier requests random shards at every epoch. Similar to the grain of cedar, the structure is rigid and fixed. Like the lines of a sonnet, every shard must fit its specific index. Any failure to return segments triggers an immediate, non-refundable slash to funds, preventing identity farming.
